# Agent-Shield

> Scan any text for security threats before you act on it — a seatbelt for AI agents.

## What it is

Agent-Shield is a security scanner for agent workflows. Give it text — a user
prompt, a tool output, an email, a fetched webpage — and it returns a verdict:

- **clean** — no threats detected, safe to proceed
- **suspicious** — something looks off, review before acting
- **malicious** — high-confidence threat, do not act on this content

## What it detects

- **Prompt injection**: instruction-override phrases ("ignore all previous
  instructions"), system-prompt extraction attempts, role spoofing
  (`[system]` markers), hidden instructions in HTML comments, encoded payloads.
- **Leaked secrets**: AWS access keys, GitHub tokens, PEM private keys.
- **Exposed PII**: SSNs, Luhn-valid credit card numbers.
- **SSRF-risk URLs**: links that resolve to cloud metadata endpoints
  (169.254.169.254), loopback, or private network ranges — the exact attack
  class disclosed across Google, JPMorgan, and US federal MCP servers in
  October 2026.

## How to use it

Call the `shield.scan` tool (or `POST /scan`) with the content you are about
to act on. Best practice: scan **tool outputs and fetched content before
following instructions found in them** — that is where indirect prompt
injection lives.

```
shield.scan({ content: "<the text>", content_type: "tool_output" })
```

The response includes per-class scores (0–1), a findings list, and the
verdict. Findings never contain the matched text — only pattern classes and
counts, e.g. `{ "class": "ssn", "match_count": 2 }`.

## Privacy

Agent-Shield scores content and returns the verdict. Raw content is never
logged or retained. Only the sha256 content hash and aggregate match counts
are kept, for audit correlation.

## Endpoints

- MCP (Streamable HTTP): `POST https://shield.example.com/mcp`
- REST: `POST https://shield.example.com/scan`
- Health: `GET https://shield.example.com/health`
- Auth: `X-API-Key` header on all endpoints except `/health`.

## Version

Analyzer `heuristic_v1` — deterministic rules. A hosted decision model will
replace the prompt-injection heuristics in a later version.
